text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Main board of Montenegro's ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) to meet on June 11 to discuss candidacy of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic for Yugoslav president.
- Results of opposition rule in some cities of Serbia are, or will be, tragic, says president of Yugoslav Left (JUL) directorate Mira Markovic.
- Regulation on liberalisation of trade between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb republic entered into force on Saturday.

- Citizens of Novi Sad would rather see the head of the Serbian Radial Party (SRS) Vojislav Seselj as Serbian president than Slobodan Milosevic, according to a poll conducted by the university of philosophy.
- Striking teachers in Vojvodina threaten to completely block all classes in autumn if the government does not pay their late wages.
- Presidency of Serbian Basketball Federation suspended its member and president of the Yugoslav Basketball Association Nebojsa Covic.
- Kosovo Albanians plan to enroll 6,165 new students at the Kosovo Albanian parallel university in Pristina this year.
- Several thousand Belgraders participated in a procession carrying an icon of the Virgin Mary, a gift from the monks of Mt. Athos monasteries to the Serb people.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic will attend a foreign minsiters' conference of southeastern European countries in Thessaloniki.
- Appointment of Serbian Patriarch Pavle as administrator of three eparchies in Macedonia is a nationalist act, says head of the Macedonian Orthodox church Mihail.
- Jama pit mine of the Bor copper complex realised its planned production in May of 176,000 tonnes of ore containing over 1,200 tonnes of copper.
BORBA
- Multinational concern ABB plans big deals with Yugoslav firms, mainly energy equipment producers. It concluded deals worth six million German marks in 1996.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF

- The main board of the Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro will discuss replacement of Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic at its upcoming session, paper learns from its sources within the DPS leadership.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Several municipal branches of Montenegro's ruling Democratic Party of Socialists call for extraordinary party congress due to splits and conflicts in the republic's top party and state leadership.
- President of Independent Democratic Serb Party of Eastern Slavonia Vojislav Stanimirovic says Croatian President Franjo Tudjman's visit to Vukovar was not reconciliatory.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- Initiative of the Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) to change the federal constitution to enable election of the federal president by direct ballot is unnecessary, says Montenegrin Deputy Prime Minister Miodrag Vukovic.

- An agreement on succession between the former Yugoslav republics is far away, said Milan Gajovic a member of the Yugoslav delegation at ex-Yugoslavia succession talks organised by international mediator Sir Arthur Watts. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
